scenarios: An executor corrects the comment to say 'counts only' and marks AC4 done, leaving the type gap unaddressed — a valid reading of the AC as written
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'asserts the escaping exception TYPE per member (or its comment is corrected to match what it does)' with 'asserts the escaping exception TYPE per member; the comment must match what the assertion now does' — making both the assertion and the comment correction mandatory.

evidence: Approach: 'Where it is (1, 3, 4), write the test the docstring already promises.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Refactor `_search_issues_calls_taking_the_default()` to accept an optional `source: str` parameter (defaulting to `_TRANSPORT_SRC.read_text()`), then call it from the teeth test with the synthetic file's source — so the teeth test exercises the predicate's detection logic on a known unpaginated caller, not the live transport's clean state.
evidence: Plan: 'the structural-guard teeth test calls the SHARED predicate `_search_issues_calls_taking_the_default()` instead of re-implementing it'
`_search_issues_calls_taking_the_default()` body at line 152: `tree = ast.parse(_TRANSPORT_SRC.read_text())` — hardcoded to the production file
The teeth test writes a synthetic unpaginated caller to `tmp_path / 'fake_transport.py'` — a path the helper will never read

Calling the helper from the teeth test would scan the live transport (currently clean), so the teeth test would PASS even if the predicate logic were completely broken — the identical vacuity the plan aims to fix
findings.finding: `_search_issues_calls_taking_the_default()` is hardcoded to scan `_TRANSPORT_SRC` (the real transport file); the plan's prescribed fix for Item 2 — 'call the shared predicate' from the teeth test — cannot work without additional refactoring because the helper always reads the live source, not the synthetic `tmp_path` file the teeth test writes.
scenarios: Implementer calls `_search_issues_calls_taking_the_default()` directly in the teeth test. The helper scans the real transport source, finds no offenders (correct implementation), and asserts `found` — but `found` is empty because the real file is clean, not because the synthetic caller was detected. The test asserts the wrong thing and the predicate can regress silently.

If someone breaks the keyword-set check in `_search_issues_calls_taking_the_default()` (e.g. changes `'maxResults'` to `'max_results_only'`), the production guard regresses but the teeth test still passes because it tests the live file, not detection capability.
findings.suggested_fix: Change `_search_issues_calls_taking_the_default(source: str | None = None)` to parse `source or _TRANSPORT_SRC.read_text()`. In the teeth test: `found = _search_issues_calls_taking_the_default(source=synthetic.read_text())` then `assert found`. This way, breaking the keyword-set logic in the helper causes the teeth test to go red.

findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'asserts the escaping exception TYPE per member (or its comment is corrected to match what it does)' with 'asserts the escaping exception TYPE per member using a specific exception class, not the broad `Exception`'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] AC3: specify that the test must call the REAL `validate_assignee_exists` implementation with only the underlying Jira-client response mocked (not the method itself), so the assertion derives from real method logic rather than a self-authored mock return value.
evidence: AC3 text: 'validate_assignee_exists is asserted to return the USERNAME STRING for both backends, not merely to exist'
No language in AC3 or the Approach section specifying that the assertion must be derived from the real method's output rather than a mock return value
The method almost certainly requires a Jira connection, making naive mocking the path of least resistance for the implementer
findings.finding: AC3 does not preclude a self-authored-oracle implementation: asserting that `validate_assignee_exists` returns a username string can be trivially satisfied by mocking the method itself to return a string and then asserting the mocked return value — a tautology identical in kind to the defects being fixed. The plan does not specify that the REAL method body must be exercised (e.g., by mocking only the underlying Jira client response, not the method under test), leaving the door open for an author to write a mock-the-return-value test that closes the AC while providing no behavioral coverage.
scenarios: Author writes: `mock_transport.validate_assignee_exists.return_value = 'jdoe'; assert transport.validate_assignee_exists('jdoe') == 'jdoe'` — test is green, method body never runs, oracle is self-authored
findings.suggested_fix: Add to AC3: 'The test must construct a real (or minimally-wrapped) transport instance, stub only the HTTP/client layer to return a synthetic Jira user object, and assert the value returned by the live method body — mocking `validate_assignee_exists` itself is explicitly prohibited as it recreates the self-authored-oracle anti-pattern.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile item (5)'s inclusion criterion: either (a) state explicitly that the plan's scope covers 'vacuous OR materially misleading' tests (broadening the title/scope statement), or (b) specify that the rename-only resolution path must still be mutation-checked (e.g. confirm the narrowed assertion fails when `BackendRegistryError` is made a subclass of `KeyError`), so AC [6] unambiguously covers it.

AC item 5 permits a 'rename' resolution with no accompanying mutation check, while AC item 6 says 'every rewritten test is mutation-checked with the mutation and verdict recorded' — these are in tension if renaming without broadening produces a test with no new mutation target
findings.finding: Item (5) is included in a plan titled 'Replace the tests that cannot fail' but the plan itself describes it as 'Real' — it can fail if `BackendRegistryError` became a subclass of `KeyError`. Its defect is name/intent mismatch, not vacuity. This makes its inclusion inconsistent with the plan's scope criterion, and the AC for (5) (`either exercises select_backend or is renamed`) does not specify a mutation check for the 'rename' branch, leaving that resolution path unverified under AC [6].
findings.location: Confirmed list item 5; Approach section ('either broaden the test or narrow the name'); AC bullet 5 ('the unknown-backend test either exercises select_backend or is renamed')
scenarios: An agent renames the test (the cheaper of the two AC-permitted options) without broadening it, satisfies the rename AC, but leaves the underlying assertion un-mutation-checked — AC [6] is then ambiguous about whether a pure rename counts as a 'rewritten test'.

A reviewer scanning the plan for 'vacuous tests' finds item (5) unexpectedly — it muddies the plan's stated criterion and risks confusion about what other 'narrower than name' tests should have been included.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to the Approach section: 'Item (5) is not strictly vacuous but is included because a name that overclaims is functionally equivalent — it hides a gap. The rename-only resolution is valid only if the renamed assertion is independently verified against the mutation that would falsify it (making BackendRegistryError a subclass of KeyError).' Then tighten AC [5] to: 'the unknown-backend test either exercises select_backend OR is renamed AND the renamed assertion is mutation-verified.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Evaluate whether `mutmut` (or an existing project mutation-testing tool) should be used to satisfy the mutation-check AC instead of the described manual approach, and explicitly record the decision (tool preferred / tool not available / manual is intentional one-off) in the plan.
evidence: Plan text: 'Each rewritten test must be MUTATION-CHECKED against the property it now claims — that is the whole point of this story'
Plan text: 'mutation-checked by adding a __repr__ that leaks it'
Plan text: 'mutation-checked by breaking that predicate and confirming the teeth test goes red'
ABSENCE: no mention of mutmut, Cosmic Ray, or any mutation-testing tool; no reference to an existing project-level mutation-testing config

Well-established prior art: mutmut (https://github.com/boxed/mutmut) is the dominant Python mutation-testing framework; Cosmic Ray is the primary alternative — both support targeted per-function runs exactly as the plan requires
findings.finding: The plan mandates 'mutation-checked' verification for every rewritten test but specifies only a manual, ad-hoc mutation discipline ('adding a `__repr__` that leaks it', 'breaking that predicate'). Established mutation-testing tooling (e.g. `mutmut` for Python) exists and is directly applicable; the plan neither considers nor dismisses it. If the project already has `mutmut` or a similar tool configured, the manual approach reinvents/duplicates that capability. If it does not, the plan silently imposes an unscalable manual process with no guidance on how results are recorded or reproduced by future contributors.
findings.location: ## Testing section; ## Acceptance criteria (all five bullet-point mutation-check requirements)
scenarios: A reviewer applying the manual mutation approach produces non-reproducible results (no CI artifact, no recorded mutant/verdict pair beyond a ticket comment)
The project already runs mutmut in CI; the manual process produces a parallel, divergent record that future maintainers cannot reconcile
A future contributor rewrites a test without knowing the manual mutation protocol, silently dropping the 'teeth' guarantee the plan was trying to establish
findings.suggested_fix: Add a single sentence to the Testing section: 'If `mutmut` is available in the project environment, run `mutmut run --paths-to-mutate <file>` and record the surviving-mutant count; otherwise apply the manual one-shot mutations described per AC and commit the before/after verdict as a comment on this ticket.' This satisfies T1(b) by showing the novel manual approach is a deliberate trade-off, not an oversight.
